meta.description: Monitor your projects' dependencies for vulnerabilities and get notified

login.title: Log in to Vectana
login.inviteOnly: Accounts are created by invitation from an administrator.

ssoErrors.not_registered: There is no account for this email. Ask an administrator to invite you.
ssoErrors.expired: The sign-in request expired. Please try again.
ssoErrors.provider: Single sign-on failed. Please try again.
ssoErrors.no_email: The identity provider did not return a verified email address.

invite.title: You're invited to Vectana
invite.description: You are creating an account for {email} at {company}.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: {group} — status of the projects you can see
dashboard.emptyHint: Add packages to a <link>project</link> to start monitoring.
dashboard.healthDescription: Most critical vulnerabilities and EOL first
dashboard.eolEmpty: Nothing has reached or is close to end of life.
dashboard.noProjects: You can't see any projects yet.

vulns.title: Vulnerabilities
vulns.description: Vulnerabilities found in the projects you can see

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Projects you can see (assigned or within your scope)
projects.name: Name
projects.departmentHint: Department heads can see and manage projects under their departments
projects.descriptionSales: Every project from the first inquiry to maintenance. Deals are shown only to sales, administrators and their members.
projects.pipelineHint: Drag a card to another column to change its stage. Each column shows its count and estimate total.
projects.statusHintInternal: Internal projects without a sale start in development or maintenance

project.scanStarted: Scanning {count} packages. Reload in a moment.

packages.drop: Drop a lockfile or SBOM to import
packages.reimportHint: Re-importing a file with the same name applies the differences
packages.importedRuntimes: {file}: {total} runtimes (added {added} / removed {removed}). See the EOL tab

members.note: Assigned members get vulnerability emails according to their settings. Partner (BP) users can only see projects they are assigned to.

webhooks.minSeverity: Notify at this severity or higher
webhooks.empty: No webhooks. Add one to notify your team's channel.

tokens.description: API tokens let CI register lockfiles and SBOMs automatically. A token can only import into this project and start a scan; it cannot view pages or change settings.
tokens.issuedOnce: Token issued. It will not be shown again once you close this, so save it to your CI secrets now.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.confirmRevoke: Revoke the token "{name}"? CI jobs using it will start failing.
tokens.exampleNote: Store the token as the repository secret {secret}. Use a different source to register SBOMs from several repositories or services into one project.

projectSettings.name: Name
projectSettings.dangerDescription: Packages, findings and webhooks are deleted too.
projectSettings.confirmDelete: Type the project name "{name}" to delete it

settings.title: Settings
settings.emailEnabled: Email me when vulnerabilities are found in projects I'm assigned to
settings.minSeverityHint: Vulnerabilities with unknown severity are always sent
settings.languageHint: Emails are sent in this language too
settings.accountsHint: Used to match the assignees of issues in linked repositories with Vectana task assignees.

users.head: Head
users.unitCostHint: Used to cost estimates. Shown only to admins, sales and accounting
users.roleHint: Pick any number. With none, the user sees only the projects they are assigned to

invitations.notSent: The email could not be sent. Share the link below instead.

eol.title: End of life
eol.description: Support status of packages and runtimes (endoflife.date)
eol.runtimesHint: Register what lockfiles don't show, such as Python, Node.js, PostgreSQL or Ubuntu. You can also drop mise.toml or .tool-versions on the Packages tab.
eol.refreshStarted: Re-checking end of life. Reload in a moment.

system.eolWarningDays: Warn this many days before end of life
system.eolWarningHint: Anything reaching end of life within this window is shown and notified as "ending soon" (1–730 days)
system.slaHint: Vulnerabilities still open or acknowledged this many days after detection count as overdue (1–3650 days)
system.reportEnabled: Email group admins, company admins and department heads a weekly summary of their organization
system.reportHint: Sent at or after the hour set on the server (09:00 Japan time by default). People who turned off email notifications are skipped.

upgrade.hint: The lowest version that fixes every unresolved (not ignored) vulnerability. Use it as a guide.

org.title: Organization dashboard
org.description: Open vulnerabilities, overdue items and days to EOL per company and department. Departments include their sub-departments.
org.slaNote: Overdue = still open or acknowledged after its own due date, or, without one, CRITICAL {critical} / HIGH {high} / MEDIUM {medium} / LOW {low} days from detection
org.partialHint: Rows marked "partial" only count the projects you can see.
org.noEol: Nothing has reached or is approaching EOL

triage.commentPlaceholder: Write a plan or findings (Ctrl/⌘+Enter to post)
triage.slaHint: No due date set, so this is the deadline from the severity SLA

estimates.description: Additional work and maintenance renewals are added as new estimates of this project.
estimates.title: Estimate
estimates.statusHint: Winning it moves a deal to Won
estimates.effortHint: With a breakdown, the rows add up instead
estimates.costHidden: Per-person unit costs and total cost are shown only to sales, administrators and accounting.

customers.title: Customers
customers.description: Client companies and their contacts. Separate from the group and partner companies under Organization.
customers.notAllowed: Only sales, administrators, accounting and PMO can see customers
customers.name: Company name
customers.companyHint: Sales handle only their own company's customers
customers.pipelineHint: Estimates add up open and won estimates of deals and running projects.
customers.projectsHint: Lost deals stay here for later analysis
customers.noProjects: No projects for this customer yet
customers.confirmDelete: Delete customer "{name}"? Customers with projects cannot be deleted.

tasks.title: Title
tasks.methodHint: Shown for the project's method ({method}). Change it in the settings.
tasks.maintenanceHint: In maintenance, this simple list replaces the Gantt chart and board. Security work at {threshold} or above lands here automatically.

gantt.unscheduled: Set a start and due date to show a task on the chart

sprints.name: Name
sprints.dodPlaceholder: e.g. Two approvals and CI green
sprints.confirmClose: Complete "{name}"? Unfinished tasks go back to the backlog.
sprints.none: No sprints yet. Create one to plan the work.
sprints.noVelocity: No sprint has been completed yet

security.thresholdHint: Vulnerabilities at this severity or above, and runtimes or packages past EOL, become tasks automatically
security.tasksHint: One task = one upgrade of a package (or runtime)
security.subject: Package / runtime
security.candidatesTitle: Below the threshold and not yet tasks
security.candidatesHint: Vulnerabilities of the same package share one task
security.noCandidates: Nothing is waiting to become a task
security.allFixed: Upgrading to {version} fixes every open vulnerability of this package.

personalTokens.title: Personal tokens (AI and scripts)
personalTokens.description: Tokens that let AI clients such as Claude, or your scripts, use Vectana with your permissions. A read-only token can view but not change anything.
personalTokens.issuedOnce: Token issued. It will not be shown again once you close this, so save it now.
personalTokens.confirmRevoke: Revoke the token "{name}"? AI clients and scripts using it will stop working.
personalTokens.mcpExample: MCP server settings (Claude Desktop, Claude Code and others)
personalTokens.mcpNote: In Claude Code you can also add it with: {command}

timesheet.title: Timesheet
timesheet.description: Enter hours per task, a week at a time. You can paste from Excel.
timesheet.emptyEditable: Start with “Add row” or “Same rows as last week”
timesheet.pasteHint: Select a cell and paste a range from Excel or a spreadsheet to fill several at once.
timesheet.pasteTooMany: Lines beyond the last row were not pasted. Add rows first.
timesheet.discard: You have unsaved hours. Discard them and move?
timesheet.nothingToCopy: All of last week's rows are already here
timesheet.taskHint: Pick a task to compare with its estimate.
timesheet.label: Work

activity.bodyPlaceholder: What was discussed, decided, and any concerns
activity.nextActionHint: The next action becomes the assignee's task and shows as the deal's next action.
activity.savedWithTask: Note saved and next action added as a task
activity.openHint: Mark them done in the task list.

actuals.description: Won estimates' effort against the hours entered (1 person-day = {hours} hours).
actuals.costHidden: Shown only to those who see unit costs
actuals.byPhaseHint: Top-level tasks with sub-tasks count as phases. Their estimate is the sum of task estimates.

billing.title: Billing
billing.description: Invoices planned from won estimates. Issue invoices in your accounting software and record here when they are sent and paid.
billing.notAllowed: This page is for accounting and administrators
billing.note: Sales plan invoices on the project's Estimates tab. Accounting and administrators record when they are sent and paid.
billing.confirmUndoInvoiced: Undo invoiced and return it to planned?
billing.dueHint: Defaults to the end of the following month.
billing.projectHint: Decide in how many installments, and when, each won estimate is billed.
billing.planHint: Split the estimate's {amount}. Invoiced and paid installments stay as they are.
billing.planMonthlyHint: List the monthly {amount} invoices month by month.

repos.description: Link a GitHub or GitLab (including self-hosted) repository to keep issues and tasks, and milestones and sprints, in step both ways. Lockfiles and SBOMs are imported on every push to the default branch and once a day.
repos.tokenHintGithub: Fine-grained token: Contents read, Issues read and write, Webhooks read and write (to register the webhook)
repos.tokenHintGitlab: Project access token with the api scope (Maintainer or above to register the webhook)
repos.securityIssues: Open issues for security tasks created automatically
repos.importPathsHint: Empty: supported files anywhere in the repository. One per line; * and ** work
repos.linked: Linked. Lockfiles and issues are being imported in the background
repos.confirmDelete: Unlink {repo}? Tasks and imported packages stay.
repos.removedSources: Removed what {count} files gone from the repository contributed
repos.manualWebhookGithub: The webhook could not be registered. Add it under the repository's Settings → Webhooks with this URL and secret (content type application/json; events: Pushes, Issues, Milestones, Pull requests).
repos.manualWebhookGitlab: The webhook could not be registered. Add it under the project's Settings → Webhooks with this URL and secret token (triggers: push, issues, merge requests).
